name: Matuku-tangotango
prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Matuku-tangotango, the underground ogre-chief of Māori legend who emerges carrying a two-handed wooden sword.
ANATOMY: ONE adult male ogre-chief in humanlike form with ONE head, TWO eyes, TWO arms, TWO legs, long visible dark hair, fully opaque plain woven flax cloak and lower garment; NO invented horns/fangs/claws or supernatural size. ONE LONG TWO-HANDED WOODEN SWORD, plain dark hardwood, held in both hands. [matuku-tangotango-c04,matuku-tangotango-c05,matuku-tangotango-c07]
MOMENT: BURST UPWARD from a VERTICAL BLACK HOLE in the ground toward viewer; his lower legs remain deep INSIDE subterranean shaft, one knee planted on rim. Both arms swing the heavy TWO-HANDED WOODEN SWORD up into attack, blade dramatically foreshortened toward viewer. His fierce wide-open roaring mouth and confrontational eyes are very close. Rough earth cascades from shoulders as he forces himself out of underground habitation. NOT a standing warrior before an ordinary horizontal cave, NOT calm pose.
POWER: Documented rising from beneath earth, NOT exploding earth magic; ordinary stones/dust shift at opening, no aura. [matuku-tangotango-c06,matuku-tangotango-c07]
SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low close angle, subject fills90% of square; natural scale unless giant explicitly documented. Important features clear at200pixels.
LIGHT & WEATHER: one dominant warm moonbreak/sunset or storm gap, strong rim light, deep walnut shadows, ordinary physical dust/moisture.
SURFACE: tactile natural fur/skin/scales where appropriate, coarse opaque textiles, rough stone, original visible painterly brushwork.
SETTING: Vertical opening of underground Putawarenuku habitation beside washing pool at dark new moon, black void below his body. [matuku-tangotango-c02,matuku-tangotango-c03]
MOOD: dangerous for hostile beings, awe-inspiring and respectful for gods/guardians, uncanny audacious for benign small spirits, never cute/calm/decorative.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text/lettering/logo/border/frame/watermark; no extra heads/limbs/fingers; no borrowed film/game/anime/comic design; no nudity or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon outlines, energy ribbons, floating runes.

artistic_choices: Dark warm palette and close low camera are editorial composition; no unsupported giant size or magic.

rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.

rejected_attempts.reason: Self-reject: mostly static ordinary warrior at cave, not active underground ogre-chief emerging; lacks strong moment.

visual_review.notes: Native and200px inspected: ogre-chief rises visibly from vertical underground hole c06/c07, both arms swing two-handed wooden sword towardviewer, long hair c04, one head/twoeyes, no invented horns/fangs or giant size. Opaque flax clothes editorial, pool nearby. Active threat and emergence clear200px, no aura/text/gore. All seven Sangar checks pass.

root_visual_review.notes: Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and face, weapon/hands, and lower-body/pit crops. What works: one adult humanlike ogre-chief with one head, two eyes and a roaring open mouth, long dark hair (matuku-tangotango-c04), and a fully opaque woven flax cloak and kilt (editorial). One knee is planted on the rim as he heaves himself out of a black pit with soil flying (rises up from beneath the earth, c06/c07). There is a pool behind (washing pool, c03), and no victim, gore, text or aura. It fails for three reasons. (1) The 'two-handed wooden sword' (c07) is drawn as a European cruciform sword carved in wood: a rectangular crossguard bar, a straight squared blade and a round pommel under the grip. That medieval Western hilt is foreign to Māori material culture, and it is the largest object in the frame. (2) Only ONE hand is visible on the grip. The other arm disappears behind the blade, so the two-handed grip the receipt claims does not read. (3) The face is a photographic portrait of an ordinary present-day Polynesian man shouting. Nothing marks him as the man-eating underground ogre-chief (c06/c09) rather than an angry warrior climbing out of a ditch, and the pit reads as a shallow hole, not an underground dwelling. A realistic Māori face cast as 'the ogre' with nothing else otherworldly also leans toward a savage-warrior stereotype. It fails the tradition/attribute check and Uji Sangar #5 and #7.

correction_notes: Keep: one humanlike ogre-chief with no invented horns, fangs, claws or giant size, long dark hair (matuku-tangotango-c04), an opaque flax cloak, a roaring confrontation with the viewer, and the moment of forcing himself up out of the earth (c06/c07) beside his washing pool (c03). Fix: (a) The weapon must be a long two-handed Māori-form hardwood striking weapon of plain dark wood, staff-like or with a flat paddle-edged blade. NO crossguard, NO pommel, NO metal, and nothing shaped like a European sword. (b) Show both hands clearly gripping the shaft. (c) Make the underground origin unmistakable. He climbs out of a deep black vertical shaft or cave mouth in the ground (Putawarenuku, c02/c09), with roots and soil streaming from his hair and cloak. Set it at dusk or night with a thin new-moon crescent visible low in the sky (c03/c06: he comes forth when the new moon appears), lit from the pool and the last light, so he reads as a creature risen from under the earth, not a man in a ditch. (d) Paint him in the house painterly style as a legendary figure with grave, earth-caked, weathered features, not a photographic portrait of a present-day man. No victim, gore, text or aura.
